sources.title: AFI Catalog: Singin' in the Rain (1952)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, history, songs, credits and dates.
supports: Gene Kelly is credited in the cast; Kelly and Stanley Donen are credited as directors.
Comden and Green described a story reflecting the film industry's transition to sound.
Most songs came from earlier MGM musicals; Make 'Em Laugh and Moses were written especially for the film.
limits: The sound-transition story is fictional and does not document one real studio's history.
The catalog's modern-source discussion contains varying accounts of the film's origin.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «Поющие под дождём» (1952)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Джин Келли—Дон Локвуд, работу со старыми песнями MGM и замысел о переходе к звуку.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The 25th Academy Awards (1953)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected film-specific nominations and categories.
supports: Jean Hagen was nominated for supporting actress.
Lennie Hayton was nominated for scoring of a musical picture.
The film had two nominations and no win in the listed categories.
limits: The page does not support an acting Oscar claim for Gene Kelly in this film.

source_link.title: Academy: 25-я церемония «Оскара» (1953)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает две номинации фильма — Джин Хейген и Ленни Хейтону, без актёрской победы Келли.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Some Like It Hot (1959)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected credits, history and production notes.
supports: Marilyn Monroe, Tony Curtis and Jack Lemmon are the leading credited cast.
The plot derives from the 1951 German film Fanfaren der Liebe.
Florida sequences were filmed at Hotel del Coronado near San Diego.
limits: The historical source relationship does not make the 1959 film a documentary.
The page's description of the title's jazz meaning is period terminology.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «В джазе только девушки» (1959)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает главных исполнителей, немецкий источник сюжета и съёмки флоридских сцен в Калифорнии.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy collection highlights: Some Like It Hot
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected overview of premise and credited creative team.
supports: Billy Wilder co-wrote the screenplay with I. A. L. Diamond.
The premise follows two musicians fleeing the mob by joining an all-female band headed to Florida.
Monroe, Curtis and Lemmon are identified as the principal stars.
limits: This Academy collection overview does not itself give a complete award ledger.

source_link.title: Academy: «В джазе только девушки» — материалы коллекции
source_link.supports: Подтверждает завязку с музыкантами, бегущими от мафии, и соавторство Уайлдера и Даймонда.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Graduate (1967)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected cast, source history, writing credits and synopsis.
supports: Dustin Hoffman is credited as Ben Braddock; Bancroft as Mrs Robinson and Ross as Elaine Robinson.
The film adapts Charles Webb's 1963 novel.
Calder Willingham and Buck Henry share screen credit; AFI reports Henry joined late to address plot issues.
limits: A synopsis is evidence of fictional plot, not a documentary account of youth culture.
Production-history details are reported history, not a substitute for source documents.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «Выпускник» (1967)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Хоффман—Бен Брэддок, роман Чарльза Уэбба как источник и авторов сценария.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: The Graduate / Point Blank
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected film overview, credits and craft description.
supports: Hoffman is identified as Benjamin Braddock, an unsettled college graduate.
The page identifies Mrs Robinson and Elaine as the other central relationship roles.
It credits Nichols's Panavision framing and Simon & Garfunkel songs, and states Nichols won Best Directing.
limits: The event description does not make Hoffman a winner; his performance was nominated at the 1968 ceremony.

source_link.title: Academy: «Выпускник» / «Выстрел в упор»
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Хоффман—Бен, ключевые отношения персонажей, работу с Panavision и победу Майка Николса за режиссуру.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: To Kill a Mockingbird (1962)
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected history, adaptation detail and setting construction notes.
supports: The film rights came from Harper Lee's 1960 novel and Horton Foote wrote the screenplay.
Gregory Peck visited Monroeville, but location filming was abandoned because it no longer resembled the Depression-era community in the novel.
Period cottages were moved to the Universal lot to construct the setting.
limits: The fictional Alabama setting and case are not a record of a real trial.
The page does not turn the film into a biography of Harper Lee or Truman Capote.

source_link.title: AFI Catalog: «Убить пересмешника» (1962)
source_link.supports: Подтверждает роман Харпер Ли как источник, сценарий Хортона Фута и создание декораций на студии.

sources.organisation: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy: To Kill a Mockingbird
sources.access_method: Direct web open; inspected premise, cast context and award record.
supports: Gregory Peck plays Depression-era lawyer Atticus Finch.
The page describes the defense of a Black man falsely accused of rape and Scout's coming-of-age viewpoint.
It records wins for Peck's acting, black-and-white art direction, and Horton Foote's adapted screenplay.
limits: The Academy's socially framed synopsis should not be treated as evidence of a particular real historical case.
The award record concerns the 1963 ceremony recognizing the 1962 release.

source_link.title: Academy: «Убить пересмешника»
source_link.supports: Подтверждает Грегори Пек—Аттикус Финч, перспективу Скаут и три конкретные победы фильма.
